subject: botany
question_text: Name different methods of vegetative reproduction in bryophytes.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.7, VSAQ 10. The book's list — fragmentation, gemma formation, budding in the secondary protonema — matches NCERT (fragmentation and gemmae in liverworts; fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema in mosses). Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Fragmentation and gemmae
lines: Fragmentation — a broken piece of the
plant body grows into a new plant.
steps.why: Vegetative reproduction copies the gametophyte without gametes. Liverworts use fragmentation of the thallus and gemmae formed inside gemma cups; mosses also fragment.
common_mistakes: Calling gemmae spores — gemmae are multicellular vegetative buds; spores come from meiosis in the capsule.
Writing 'gamete formation' — that is sexual reproduction, not vegetative.
steps.memory_tip: Gemma sounds like gem — picture small green gems sitting in open cups on the thallus.
steps.margin_note: Name each method; one bracket example (Marchantia) is a safe extra.

steps.label: Budding in the secondary protonema

lines.text: Also: budding in the secondary protonema

lines: In mosses the secondary protonema forms
buds that grow into new gametophores.
steps.why: Mosses add a third method: the secondary protonema, produced during vegetative reproduction, carries buds that develop into leafy gametophores.
common_mistakes: Writing 'primary protonema' — the budding named under vegetative reproduction is in the secondary protonema.
steps.memory_tip: Three methods in order F–G–B: fragmentation, gemmae, budding in the secondary protonema.
steps.margin_note: Naming all three methods is the safe full answer.

insider_note: The book lists exactly these three methods; the word 'secondary' before protonema is the detail examiners check.
